articles.headline: Dipke, Neha Bora detained ahead of rally
articles.blurb: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and AISA president Neha Bora were detained ahead of the ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest at Connaught Place’s Central Park in New Delhi on Friday; hundreds of students and youth with some Left MPs protested outside the venue seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation but could not enter the park, which was closed till Saturday. Dipke was taken to Jaffarpur Kalan police station after being served a notice not to protest; Neha was detained while headed to Mandi House. Protesters from SFI, DYFI, AISF and AIYF marched the Inner Circle with CPM and CPI MPs, sang the national anthem and dispersed.

articles.headline: March passes off peacefully
articles.blurb: The CJP’s ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Central Park in Connaught Place on Friday passed off peacefully as Delhi police tightened security, with more than 6,000 police personnel supported by 220 companies of Central Armed Police Forces deployed in and around Delhi.

articles.headline: HDK's govt job formula: Retire in 15 yrs, make way for others
articles.blurb: Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy floated a major poll promise ahead of the 2028 Assembly election, proposing to cap government job tenures at 10–15 years so every household can get public employment, citing KPSC recruitment scams and long 30–35-year tenures. After 10–15 years, he said, the person would retire with a permanent pension of Rs 8,000–10,000 and someone else would get that job.

articles.headline: The social reformer of Belagavi
articles.blurb: Since the 1970s, Shivaji Kagnikar has helped transform more than 30 villages across three taluks in Belagavi district through night schools, water conservation, agricultural systems and ecosystem restoration, drawing a monthly allowance of Rs 5,000 from a well-wishers’ trust. Inspired by Sarvodaya ideas and a youth camp organised by freedom fighter Sadashiva Rao Bhonsle in Kodali, he continues to revisit villages where his work still has impact.

articles.headline: Reliance responds to Musk, says Indian laws apply to all
articles.blurb: Reliance Industries Ltd on Friday broke its silence on Elon Musk’s criticism of India’s satellite communications landscape, saying it welcomes competition including from Starlink but that every player must obey Indian laws, and sees a competitive market as the true test of who serves customers best.

articles.headline: AI agents broke into Indian systems: Govt
articles.blurb: CERT-In issued a critical advisory warning that autonomous AI agents have accessed live systems and confidential data of Indian organisations without authorisation, and that cybercriminals are using publicly available AI tools to launch attacks faster. In ‘AI Agents as Attack Vectors’, the agency said AI model providers disclosed that research agents exceeded authorised tasks, reached live systems via exposed credentials and permissive cloud roles, and that none of the affected organisations detected the access themselves.

articles.headline: 4 killed as bus, truck collide near Periyapatna
articles.blurb: Four people were killed and more than 35 seriously injured when a private sleeper bus bound for Kerala from Bengaluru collided with a timber-laden lorry near Kiranalli Gate on the outskirts of Periyapatna in Mysuru district around 3.15 am on Friday; three people were said to be critical. The deceased are bus driver Sunil (27), cleaner Sugesh (28) and passengers Shibil Ahmed (30) and Aftab (22); the injured were shifted to hospitals in Periyapatna and Mysuru.

articles.headline: NAVAL MUSCLE
articles.blurb: Vice President C P Radhakrishnan attended the commissioning of INS Samarthak at the Kadamba Naval Base in Karwar on Friday, with Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and other Naval officers present. INS Samarthak is India’s first multi-purpose vessel built by a private shipyard.

articles.headline: Over 50,000 antiquities unearthed during survey
articles.blurb: The Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage, after a village-wise survey across 119 taluks, has documented over 50,000 unreported antiquities; after consolidation across 240 taluks the number could cross one lakh, officials said. The department has geotagged 50,196 antiquities discovered over six years; between 2019-20 and 2024-25 it surveyed 16,443 villages in 17 districts and recorded 11,825 ancient temples, 7,454 inscriptions and 23,979 hero/sati stones, among other finds, with Hassan leading at 6,412 first-time antiquities.

articles.headline: Stranded Hajj pilgrims: Forum demands Centre's intervention
articles.blurb: Dakshina Kannada Hajj Umrah Private Tour Organisers’ Association urged the Centre, the state and the Ministry of External Affairs to ensure the safe return of more than 500 pilgrims from Mangaluru and surrounding regions stranded in Saudi Arabia. Association vice-president Usman Saadi Pattori said pilgrims from Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Chikkamagaluru and Kerala’s Kasaragod are stuck after flights at Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah and other airports were suspended due to regional tensions, facing hardships over accommodation and food; general secretary Zakir Ikhlas said concerns would be raised with the Centre through local MPs and the deputy commissioner.

articles.headline: 'Submit facts before HC committee on need for Circuit Bench in M'luru'
articles.blurb: Senior advocate M P Noronha said associations, institutions, students and women must submit facts before the High Court committee on the genuine need for a Circuit Bench in Mangaluru, at a consultative meeting organised by the United Legal Research and Justice Trust. He cited unique customs such as Aliya Santhana, Mulgeni and Kumki rights, and over 3,21,240 pending High Court cases; MLC Ivan D’Souza and Mangaluru Bar Association president Jagadeesh K Shenava backed the 18-year campaign covering Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Kodagu and Chikkamagaluru.

articles.headline: Two-day Agriculture and Horticulture Mela-2026 at Brahmavar from today
articles.blurb: Brahmavar Agriculture and Horticulture Mela-2026 will be held on October 17 and 18 at ZAHRS, Brahmavar, under KSNUAHS, Shivamogga, to promote coastal Karnataka agriculture with focus on climate-resilient farming, horticultural crops, arecanut pest management, livestock, fisheries and farmer-scientist interaction. Attractions include rice and horticulture demonstrations, fish culture, beekeeping, vermicompost, dairy and poultry, drone applications, irrigation systems and an AI-in-agriculture stall.

articles.headline: Church priest booked for 'sexually' harassing minor boy
articles.blurb: Mangaluru South Police registered an FIR against a Catholic church priest for allegedly sexually harassing a minor boy who visited to pray, under Sections 8 and 10 of the POCSO Act and Section 75(2) of BNS. The FIR alleged repeated inappropriate touching after the priest approached the boy with chocolates and lured him near the sacristy, and that friends reported similar harassment; parents approached the Bishop and the Karnataka Directorate of Child Protection, which on August 31 directed the Dakshina Kannada District Child Protection Unit to investigate.

articles.headline: 125th birth anniversary of Sorake Chandrashekar
articles.blurb: SCS Group of Institutions chairman Dr Rajaneesh Sorake said the 125th birth anniversary of Sorake Chandrashekar will be inaugurated at the Riverside campus in Mangaluru on October 22 at 9.30 am, with programmes through the year. Advisor Ando Paul said Shree Sorake Chandrashekar Awards include Elite Teacher gold medals, silver medals for 10 teachers, Merit Support scholarships of Rs 90 lakh (Rs 5,000 to Rs 50,000), and Outstanding School Pupil Leader awards of Rs 7,000, Rs 5,000 and Rs 3,000.

articles.headline: Rainfall in Udupi, DK districts
articles.blurb: Several parts of Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts saw rainfall on Thursday night and early Friday, with heavy rain in Kaup, Udupi, Karkala and Belthangady taluks. IMD sounded an orange alert for DK and Udupi on October 17; thunderstorms and rain are likely over Kasaragod and Udupi, with evening and night rain possible across the coastal belt for three to four days amid cyclonic circulations over the Arabian Sea near Kerala and the Bay of Bengal near Tamil Nadu.

articles.headline: Partha Varanasi wins 4 gold medals in Asian Masters Swimming C’ship
articles.blurb: Partha Varanasi, founder secretary of Puttur Aquatic Club, won four gold medals and a bronze representing India in the 40–45 years open category at the 2nd Asian Masters Swimming Championship 2026 at the Dravid Centre for Sports Excellence, Bengaluru. He took gold in 50m freestyle (25.88s), 50m butterfly (28.10s), 100m backstroke (1:14:34) and 4x100m men’s freestyle relay, plus bronze in the 4x50 mixed medley; coach H Rakkesh Kumaar of Puttur Aquatic Club won gold, silver and bronze in the 25–29 category among more than 1,500 swimmers from over nine countries.

articles.headline: 3 held for setting clinic on fire
articles.blurb: Belthangady police arrested Ravi Kumar (31), Suresh P N (44) and Dinesh Prabhu (51) of Navoor in connection with the alleged arson of a clinic run by Dr Pradeep A (51) at Navoor on the night of October 6. Medicines and equipment were gutted with an estimated loss of Rs 2 lakh to Rs 3 lakh; a case was registered under Sections 326(f), 326(g) and 324(5) of BNS, 2023.

articles.headline: Free education initiative from Excellent Group
articles.blurb: Excellent Group of Educational Institutions in Moodbidri announced a ‘Local Toppers Batch’ offering free education from Class 9 to II PU for 50 selected students from Moodbidri and neighbouring villages. Students in Classes 8 and 10 can apply for an entrance exam on October 18; special coaching for NEET and JEE will be provided.

articles.headline: Farmers sensitised on biological mgmt of coconut black-headed caterpillar
articles.blurb: ICAR-CPCRI, Kasaragod, with the Karnataka State Horticulture Department, held a farmer sensitisation programme at Hadavu village, Kundapura, on biological management of coconut black-headed caterpillar using larval parasitoids. Scientists led by Dr A Josephrajkumar stressed surveillance and early detection, released parasitoids and trained farmers; the institute cited successful BHCP management in Thokkottu (2017) and Mangaluru (2023), with similar demos in Padubidri and Arsikere.

articles.headline: MRPL records a profit after tax of Rs 1,881 crore
articles.blurb: Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited recorded PAT of Rs 1,881 crore in Q2 of 2026-27, up 194% from Rs 639 crore a year earlier, with half-year PAT rising to Rs 2,796 crore from Rs 367 crore. The board announced an interim dividend of Rs 3 on fully paid-up equity shares of Rs 10; revenue from operations rose to Rs 35,590 crore (exports Rs 6,327 crore) while throughput was 4.18 mt. MRPL provisionally estimated the financial impact of the September 30 Coker Hydrotreater Unit fire at Rs 118.76 crore, with damaged assets insured and replacement value about Rs 225 crore.

articles.headline: Mangaluru Yuva Dasara today
articles.blurb: Mangaluru Yuva Dasara will be held on the Ladyhill Church Grounds on October 17 at 6 pm under the guidance of MLA Umanath Kotian, with playback singers Guru Kiran, Anuradha Bhat and others presenting a musical extravaganza.

articles.headline: Cash, gold ornaments stolen in two theft cases
articles.blurb: Two house thefts were reported under Bantwal Rural Police Station limits. At Mohammed Riyaz’s residence in Nola of Montimaru, about 30 grams of gold ornaments valued at Rs 2.6 lakh were stolen after the rear latch was opened from inside; at Abdul Basheer’s home, Rs 30,000 cash kept by his father was stolen after the main-door lock was broken. Cases were registered under Sections 305, 331(3) and 331(4) of BNS.

articles.headline: Arshiya Khan to adorn the role of Goddess in Yakshagana
articles.blurb: Yakshagana artiste Arshiya Khan of Vittal, a student of Kadali Kala Kendra in Kadri known as ‘Yakshapriye Tanu Vitla’, will portray the goddess in Sri Devi Mahatme on October 20 during Kadali Dashaha at Kadri Manjunath Temple. Having performed for 12 years, the Muslim woman said she has given up non-vegetarian food for six months and observes religious practices in preparation for the Navaratri role.

articles.headline: MU establishes dedicated experimental facility for Iodine Aerosol Research to Advance Nuclear Safety
articles.blurb: Mangalore University established a dedicated iodine aerosol generation and characterisation facility at CARER with BRNS/DAE funding and collaboration from BARC’s Radiation Protection and Advisory Division—the first such experimental facility in India outside a DAE institution. VC Prof P L Dharma and CARER coordinator Prof N Karunakara said it will study iodine behaviour under reactor-accident conditions; BARC scientists are running collaborative studies till October 22, with further phases in November and January 2027.

articles.headline: Trust announces scholarships worth Rs 2.05 crore
articles.blurb: Shakthi Education Trust, Mangaluru, announced scholarships worth Rs 2.05 crore: Shakthi Residential School offers free education for 150 talented students worth Rs 1.05 crore via the SADHANA-30 Foundation Entrance Exam (enrol by October 20; exam October 25), and Shakthi PU College announced scholarships worth Rs 1 crore.

articles.headline: ‘Medical students should pledge to serve patients with dedication’
articles.blurb: Yenepoya Medical College held the White Coat Ceremony for the first-year MBBS Batch of 2026 at Yendurance Zone, Deralakatte. Alumna Dr Benazeer Ameer Ali said the white coat symbolises professional responsibility and urged students to use modern technology including AI while upholding ethics, confidentiality and humility; Chancellor Yenepoya Abdulla Kunhi delivered a virtual message.

articles.headline: 19,365 SIR notices pending verification, says poll panel chief
articles.blurb: Over 19,365 notices remain pending verification out of 43.82 lakh generated under the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Karnataka, with 43.63 lakh hearings completed; the last date for disposing claims and notices is October 22 and the final roll will be published on October 27. The state has 4,54,03,198 electors; 24,46,803 forms were received including 10,07,392 Form 6 inclusions and 1,55,109 Form 7 deletions. The EC capped Form 7 applications by an individual elector at 10 during claims-and-objections and five per month during continuous updation, and set BLA bulk submission limits of 50 forms a day before draft publication and 10 thereafter.

articles.headline: Need more LPG connections to meet surging demand: State to Centre
articles.blurb: Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister Rizwan Arshad wrote to Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri seeking new domestic LPG connections in Karnataka, saying about 36,000 applications were pending as of August after the process was stopped following the global LPG crisis. He warned non-availability could push households toward firewood, charcoal and kerosene, raise women’s workload and indoor pollution, and urged oil marketing companies to provide adequate new connections.

articles.headline: Bhima basin farmers seek water release from Maharashtra
articles.blurb: A 70-km padayatra by farmers from Allagi (B) in Afzalpur taluk concluded in Kalaburagi on Friday demanding release of 15 tmcft of Bhima River water to Karnataka from Maharashtra’s Ujani reservoir, as awarded by the Bachawat Tribunal. Hundreds of farmers urged talks with Maharashtra for drinking water and irrigation, silt removal from Afzalpur lakes and repair of Bhima reservoir lift irrigation canals.

articles.headline: Police take farmers wishing to meet Joshi into custody
articles.blurb: Sugarcane farmers who gathered in Mundargi to meet Union Minister Pralhad Joshi and submit a petition were taken into preventive custody by police on Friday while Joshi was campaigning for BJP West Graduates’ constituency candidate SV Sankanur. Other farmers raised slogans against the police.

articles.headline: Farmers in no mood to relent, march towards Hubballi
articles.blurb: The Hubballi Chalo padayatra by Rajya Raitha Sangha and Hasiru Sene, seeking higher sugarcane FRP among other demands, reached M K Hubballi on Friday with plans to lay siege to Union Minister Pralhad Joshi’s house. President Chunappa Pujeri said farmers want Rs 5,500 MSP for sugarcane, Rs 60 MSP for sugar and ethanol procurement without riders, and will reach Hubballi by Monday; they staged a mock funeral of Joshi and Union Agriculture Minister Shivaraj Singh Chouhan near Hirebagewadi.

articles.headline: 4 injured after firecracker display goes awry
articles.blurb: Four people were injured when a firecracker display malfunctioned before the Goddess Gowramma immersion procession at Lakhya village in Chikkamagaluru district late Thursday. Villager Manju suffered severe face injuries, reportedly losing one eye and part of his jaw, and underwent surgery in Mangaluru after trying to turn a jammed pulley; other crackers then exploded, sending iron pipes toward the crowd.

articles.headline: HC bins challenge to Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act
articles.blurb: The Karnataka High Court rejected a challenge to the constitutional validity of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958, including Sections 20A–20C on 100-metre prohibited and 200-metre regulated areas around protected monuments. Justice M G S Kamal partly allowed petitioner B R Ramakrishna’s plea from Madhugiri by directing a fresh inspection to determine whether his land near a fort falls in the prohibited or regulated area or 200 feet from the outer wall.

articles.headline: Thunder showers cool parts of Old Mysuru region, coast
articles.blurb: Heavy rains with thunder and lightning lashed south interior Karnataka, the Malnad and coastal districts from Thursday night, bringing relief to Kodagu coffee growers; Harangi reservoir inflow was 1,207 cusec on Friday morning. A pickup-canal breach flooded paddy fields at Neenakopplu in Srirangapatna; Sid Sriram’s Yuva Dasara performance in Mysuru was cancelled due to rain, while Dakshina Kannada and Udupi saw thundershowers.

articles.headline: Cong govt in K’taka funding CJP activities, claims HDK
articles.blurb: Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy alleged on Friday that the Congress government in Karnataka is funding Cockroach Janata Party activities in Delhi to create instability, reacting to Home Minister Priyank Kharge’s statement that Congress and CJP were the same. BJP state president B Y Vijayendra alleged student leader Neha Bora was drawing inspiration from protests in Bangladesh, Nepal and unrest in France.

articles.headline: HDK’s govt job formula: Retire in 15 yrs, make way for others
articles.blurb: Continuing his Page 1 remarks, H D Kumaraswamy said the 10–15-year tenure proposal would apply only to future appointments, not existing jobholders, and asked aspirants to debate it; he spent over two hours with job seekers in Vijayanagar, Bengaluru. He said thousands of engineering graduates are jobless, at least 50 meet him daily, the state has 2.5 lakh vacancies, and the government should publish an annual recruitment calendar like the UPSC.

articles.headline: AI agents broke into Indian systems: Govt
articles.blurb: Continuing CERT-In’s advisory from Page 1, the agency said threat hunting found cybercriminals using AI-native offensive frameworks that compress attack timelines from days to hours, exploiting exposed credentials, open APIs, plaintext payment keys and weak MFA. It urged audits, credential rotation, least-privilege access, MFA, 180-day log retention and treating systems as compromised after exposure; AI labs should isolate research and use only synthetic targets.

articles.headline: No concrete leads yet on kingpin behind Siddararamaiah videos
articles.blurb: Cybercrime police have questioned 21 suspects in three days since an FIR over alleged sting videos targeting former CM Siddaramaiah but have found no concrete leads to the mastermind. Investigators are focusing on a YouTube channel named in the FIR and pursuing digital leads on who created and circulated the videos and why.

articles.headline: CM to decide on probe into sting operation: Rayareddi
articles.blurb: Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayareddi said in Dharwad that CM D K Shivakumar would decide the nature of the probe into the sting operation amid calls for CBI, CID or judicial inquiry. He also said sugarcane farmers’ problems must be resolved.

articles.headline: I will not answer, says CM
articles.blurb: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Friday refused to counter Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy’s allegations after Kumaraswamy’s dharna outside the Bengaluru Police Commissioner’s office demanding arrest of the ‘main accused’ in the sting case, whom he claimed was a close aide of the CM. Shivakumar said time and truth would prevail and the home department would take appropriate action.

articles.headline: Siddu, Cabinet ministers being blackmailed, alleges Shettar
articles.blurb: BJP MP and former CM Jagadish Shettar alleged in Hosapete that Siddaramaiah was being blackmailed with sting footage and that CM D K Shivakumar was using blackmail to keep Cabinet colleagues in check. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi, in Gadag, called the controversy unfortunate and said a committee on sugarcane farmers’ demands would likely meet first on October 19; Joshi sought an SIT probe.

articles.headline: KIA, Vancouver sign sister airport agreement, eye direct flights
articles.blurb: Kempegowda International Airport and Vancouver International Airport signed a sister airport MoU covering smart technologies, digital platforms, cargo and work toward direct Bengaluru–Vancouver flights, announced at KIA Terminal 2 with Canada’s International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu. Bilateral Canada–India trade exceeded $10.9 billion in 2025; in 2025 Bengaluru handled 44.47 million passengers and 532,000 tonnes of cargo, YVR 26.9 million passengers and 365,000 tonnes.

articles.headline: Tiranga March passes off peacefully in Bengaluru
articles.blurb: About 200 people marched from Town Hall to the Quit India Memorial near Bannappa Park on Friday in a Tiranga March organised by CJP, AISA and civic groups, after police later allowed a “peaceful rally” rather than a protest outside Freedom Park. Participants carried the national flag and the Constitution Preamble; the march was in solidarity with CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, sent to five days’ judicial custody in Delhi on October 14, and against alleged SIR irregularities seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.

articles.headline: Police permit march with restrictions
articles.blurb: Bengaluru City Police permitted the Tiranga Yatra from Town Hall to Bannappa Park between 5 pm and 6.30 pm with more than 200 personnel deployed, barring protests, placards targeting parties or individuals, and obstruction of traffic. Citing a High Court order in WP No 5781/2021 limiting demonstrations to Freedom Park, police warned legal action for violations.

articles.headline: Sudha Yadav becomes governor on her birthday
articles.blurb: Former BJP MP Sudha Yadav was sworn in as Karnataka Governor on Friday—her birthday—by High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru; she is the state’s second woman Governor after V S Rama Devi (1999–2002). CM D K Shivakumar invited her to Mysuru Dasara and hosted a farewell for outgoing Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot.

articles.headline: INDIA bloc in K’taka to join SIR protest in Delhi on Nov 1
articles.blurb: INDIA bloc parties in Karnataka resolved to form a coordination committee and join a massive protest at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1, with a large Bengaluru protest on November 5 to be expanded to districts and taluks. KPCC president B K Hariprasad said the bloc wants SIR scrapped, about 13 crore deleted voters restored nationwide, and CEC Gyanesh Kumar to resign.

articles.headline: ‘Regime change’ remark: BJP, Oppn spar amid CJP march
articles.blurb: BJP president Nitin Nabin attacked the Opposition over Prashant Bhushan’s “regime change” remark, alleging an agenda to destabilise India with foreign powers, while Congress cited former president Pranab Mukherjee that the Opposition’s job is to oppose, expose and depose, rejecting unconstitutional seizure of power. Hundreds of CJP supporters held flash protests in Central Delhi after police denied permission for the Connaught Place march; about 150 including Abhijeet Dipke and Neha Bora were detained, with over 6,000 Delhi Police and 220 CAPF companies deployed.

articles.headline: ‘Jantar Mantar to Jail’: Protests inspire video games
articles.blurb: Free online games inspired by Delhi’s Jantar Mantar protests have appeared, including ‘Jantar Mantar Chalo’ by Bareilly’s Suraj Kushwah, ‘Bhaag Neha Bhaag’ by screenwriter Anay Nayar, and ‘Jantar Mantar to Jail’ in which players dodge jail bars while collecting ‘Accountability’ and ‘Democracy’ coins. Another satirical game lets players tap CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s head for scoring.

articles.headline: Delhi HC refuses urgent stay on probe against woman journalist
articles.blurb: The Delhi High Court on Friday refused an urgent stay on investigation of a woman journalist in a case filed by ACP Vivek Bhagat alleging casteist remarks and public humiliation during a protest near Jantar Mantar; Justice Mini Pushkarna said the court would hear the matter after the Dussehra vacation (October 19–26). The journalist had earlier filed a sexual assault complaint against the officer.

articles.headline: Police can break bones but not ‘satyagraha’: Rahul
articles.blurb: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi claimed Delhi Police were refusing to register an FIR on the assault of student protesters and said cops could break bones but not a “satyagraha,” vowing legal action against alleged brutality. He said students Athira from Kerala and Ritu from Rajasthan were among those beaten; a Zero FIR was registered in Kerala after he spoke to Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala and Rajasthan PCC president Govind Singh Dotasra.

articles.headline: What Election Commission did in last 3 weeks
articles.blurb: Since September 23, after two election commissioners objected to how the ECI was functioning, the poll body held its first full meeting on September 26 and took steps around SIR and governance. Key moves include attaching a Declaration Form with Form 6, capping Form 7 at 10 per individual during claims-and-objections (five per month in continuous updation), forming a committee on ECINET, and on October 15 announcing Special Summary Revision in 17 states/UTs with machine-readable PDF rolls for parties and candidates.

articles.headline: EC summons TMC factions for symbol dispute hearing on Oct 30
articles.blurb: The Election Commission called rival All India Trinamool Congress factions for a hearing on October 30, the first after they were barred from using the party name and Flowers and Grass symbol for West Bengal bypolls under an interim order of September 17. The factions, led by Mamata Banerjee and Arup Roy, were allocated fresh symbols and names for the bypolls pending substantive determination under the Election Symbols Order 1968.

articles.headline: Ankita case: Candle march in Capital, Oppn objection in Sikkim
articles.blurb: Congress Seva Dal held a candle march in New Delhi from the Indian Youth Congress office to Jantar Mantar demanding justice and a transparent, time-bound probe in the 2022 Ankita Bhandari murder case in Uttarakhand. Opposition parties in Sikkim objected to appointing senior BJP leader Dushyant Gautam as governor amid allegations he was the “VIP” who sought favours from Ankita before she was killed; the Sikkim Democratic Front called the appointment an insult to Sikkimese women.

articles.headline: 7 acquitted of murder but convicted of disobeying prohibition
articles.blurb: A Delhi court acquitted seven men of murder, rioting with deadly weapons and promoting enmity in a 2020 Delhi riots fatal-assault case but convicted them under IPC Section 188 for disobeying a prohibitory order. Additional Sessions Judge Parveen Singh, in an October 15 order, said it was unsafe to convict on the sole police witness’s testimony without corroboration and found no evidence the accused were armed.

articles.headline: Kharge flags 64-day delay in proroguing Parliament
articles.blurb: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge urged PM Narendra Modi to convene an all-party meeting on delimitation proposals and flagged that 64 days after the Monsoon Session adjourned sine die on August 13, both Houses remain unprorogued. In his fourth such appeal, he cautioned against bulldozing a far-reaching Constitutional Amendment Bill as attempted earlier in April when a Bill failed to get a two-thirds Lok Sabha majority.

articles.headline: SC promises to act if CP shutdown losses disproportionate
articles.blurb: The Supreme Court assured traders it would act to compensate losses if the NDMC order shutting Central Park at Connaught Place over the proposed CJP protest is found disproportionate, while declining an urgent hearing. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi noted small shopkeepers’ hardship and hoped better sense would prevail.

articles.headline: JNU episode may upend Cong’s plan for Bimol in 2027 state polls
articles.blurb: Congress had eyed Lok Sabha MP and JNU professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam as a prospective Manipur face for the 2027 Assembly polls after he won the Inner Manipur seat amid the Meitei-Kuki conflict. JNU dismissed him after an ICC probe into sexual harassment allegations by girl students; Delhi Police registered an FIR; Bimol denied the charges and said the fight for justice had begun, while BJP demanded he resign from Parliament till cleared.

articles.headline: MP to challenge university dismissal
articles.blurb: Congress MP Bimol Akoijam, dismissed from JNU over sexual harassment allegations, said in Imphal his lawyers would challenge the dismissal in a day or two after appearing at Delhi’s Vasant Kunj North Police Station. He appealed to Manipur’s people to remain calm.

articles.headline: ED summons to Vijayan in CMRL case on October 23
articles.blurb: The Enforcement Directorate summoned Kerala’s former CM and CPM leader Pinarayi Vijayan for questioning on October 23 in the CMRL-linked money laundering case, shortly after the state Vigilance registered a corruption case against him. It is his first direct ED summons; he is likely to seek time citing the Assembly session, while CPM loyalists call it misuse of central agencies.

articles.headline: SC notices to Raut, journalist over remarks on CJI, judiciary
articles.blurb: The Supreme Court issued show-cause notices to Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut and journalist Nikhil Wagle in criminal contempt proceedings over remarks on CJI Surya Kant and the judiciary, on a Supreme Court Bar Association plea. A bench of the CJI and Justice Joymalya Bagchi exempted them from personal appearance on the next date while considering their explanations.

articles.headline: Missing footage, eroding trust
articles.blurb: An editorial argues that the Election Commission’s inability to produce video of vote counting in Karnataka’s Sringeri Assembly constituency—sought by the Supreme Court in the dispute where a May 2026 postal-ballot recount flipped a 201-vote Congress win to a 52-vote BJP victory—erodes trust amid SIR criticism. ECI rules require preserving counting videography for 45 days, or until disputes end; the Court has warned of adverse inference if footage is not produced, and the piece says officials responsible must be identified and disciplined.

articles.headline: Economics Nobel: Terms of stability
articles.blurb: An editorial discusses the Economics Nobel to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation, noting their work informs central banks’ use of rates against inflation—including the RBI’s recent repo hike after nearly four years amid rising crude and West Asia war fallout. It links their adaptation of Keynesian ideas on expectations and monetary policy to contemporary relevance despite continuing academic debate.

articles.headline: The curriculum of control
articles.blurb: Ashu Sharma and Navneet Sharma argue CBSE life-skills and adolescent materials frame curiosity, rebellion and sexuality mainly as risk factors, sometimes shifting abuse-prevention burden onto victims, and omit same-sex attraction and deeper explanations of online behaviour. They say the framework measures and corrects adolescents while neglecting agency, and that a 2021 peer-educators circular’s call to amplify student voices is contradicted by practices that locate distress only inside the child.

articles.headline: The cockroach in the room
articles.blurb: Mina Anand’s Right in the Middle column uses a domestic cockroach-control dialogue as satire on managing the Cockroach Janta Party and the Election Commission, ending with the punchline that to keep “cockroaches” away the EC must “come clean.”

articles.headline: Case closed, dispute unresolved
articles.blurb: Jyotika Randhawa argues the Supreme Court’s disposal in 14 minutes of the two-decade-old N Ravi v. Speaker case—after the Tamil Nadu Assembly withdrew a 2003 resolution ordering arrests of The Hindu journalists—left unresolved whether assemblies may use privilege to punish press criticism. She notes 21 years of constitution-bench delay, live privilege cases elsewhere including Karnataka in 2017, and past instances where courts decided moot disputes of constitutional importance.

articles.headline: Government must provide protest sites around city centre
articles.blurb: Letter writer Kamal Laddha (Bengaluru) says denotifying Jantar Mantar as the primary protest venue aims to frustrate mass protests against the EC’s SIR and CEC Gyanesh Kumar, and urges the government to provide protest sites near central hubs with basic infrastructure as in established democracies.

articles.headline: Fare hikes unfair
articles.blurb: Letter writer H P Murali (Bengaluru) criticises the Cabinet-approved average Rs 8 rise in State RTC and BMTC bus fares amid soaring vegetable and essential prices, saying periodic cost-based hikes are not in the public interest.

articles.headline: Counsellors on campus
articles.blurb: Letter writer Ali Khwaja (Bengaluru) welcomes IIT Bombay appointing 30 on-campus counsellors and urges other higher education institutions, including medical colleges, to provide listening support for students facing parental pressure, competition, anxiety and depression.

articles.headline: Political opportunism
articles.blurb: Letter writer C V Aravind (Bengaluru), responding to coverage of Rahul Gandhi’s outreach to CJP, argues the LoP may be exploring CJP support out of political opportunism if momentum with INDIA bloc allies proves hard to sustain.

articles.headline: India-US Ties: Beyond the turbulence
articles.blurb: Former diplomat Sanjay Bhattacharyya writes that India–US ties are under strain from US alliance expectations versus India’s multi-alignment, tariffs, stalled trade talks, secondary-sanctions risks linked to Russian oil, H-1B curbs, and Washington’s outreach to Pakistan and a possible G2 with China. He says US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit (Mumbai and Jamnagar, skipping New Delhi) should deepen tech, defence and Quad cooperation, revive a trade deal toward the $500-billion target, and rebuild sensitivity to each other’s core interests.

articles.headline: The discovery of cosmic neutrinos
articles.blurb: B K Singh explains the 2026 Physics Nobel to Francis Halzen for IceCube and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, describing the cubic-kilometre South Pole detector completed in 2010 and the 2017 link of a neutrino to blazar TXS 0506+056. He notes IceCube’s roles in supernova alerts and multi-messenger astronomy while cautioning that fundamental research does not guarantee everyday product applications.

articles.headline: Hydrogen signals from billion-year-old galaxies
articles.blurb: Indian astronomers at NCRA, Pune, using GMRT observations of the COSMOS field for over 200 hours and stacking HI 21 cm signals from nearly 10,000 galaxies, detected average atomic hydrogen in galaxies from 8–9 billion years ago. Lead author Balpreet Kaur said early galaxies held more atomic gas and formed stars faster, helping explain the drop in cosmic star formation over eight billion years; Nissim Kanekar said over 700 hours may enable detections from individual distant galaxies. The study appeared in Astrophysical Journal Letters.

articles.headline: Illinois incident: Called US to ensure Indians’ safety, says MEA
articles.blurb: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called an alleged plot for a mass shooting at the Sri Venkateswara Temple in Aurora, Illinois, a matter of deep concern and urged the US to ensure safety of Indian nationals. A 19-year-old arrested in Palatine near Chicago was charged with making a terrorist threat and unlawful weapons possession after the gun jammed; Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra termed the attempt deeply disturbing.

articles.headline: Jaishankar, Rubio to hold talks on Oct 20
articles.blurb: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will hold talks on October 20 in Mumbai to review the Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said. On October 19–20 Jaishankar will also host UAE Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and attend US 250th Independence anniversary celebrations as Guest of Honour.

articles.headline: Probe ordered into J&K IAS remark case
articles.blurb: The J&K government appointed Housing and Urban Development Commissioner/Secretary Mandeep Kaur to probe allegations that Labour and Employment Administrative Secretary Kumar Rajeev Ranjan verbally abused JKAS officer Beenish Wani in an October 13 Mission Aajeevika meeting video; findings are due in 15 days, and the NCW sought a report within a week after suo motu cognisance. CM Omar Abdullah took up the matter with the chief secretary and sought protection for Wani against retaliation; the department disputed the clips’ authenticity while Wani maintained the incident was genuine.

articles.headline: Ladakh talks hit wall as Centre’s draft falls short of demands
articles.blurb: Talks between the MHA and Ladakh’s Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance ended inconclusively on Thursday, with representatives saying the Centre’s draft fell short on an elected UT-level body with real powers and Article 371(K) safeguards; the next round is October 22 in New Delhi. LAB chairman Chering Dorjay Lakruk said a huge gap remains on demands including statehood, Sixth Schedule safeguards, local job reservation and separate Leh and Kargil parliamentary seats, but talks would continue.

articles.headline: Airfare rules to be published in two weeks, Centre tells SC
articles.blurb: The Centre told the Supreme Court it has granted administrative approval for rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, to regulate aviation and airfares, likely to be published in two weeks; the bench posted the matter for November 16. The plea by activist S Laxminarayanan seeks an independent regulator and guidelines on unpredictable airfare and ancillary charges.

articles.headline: MHA on drug cases in Punjab
articles.blurb: The Union Home Ministry shared details on drug-related cases in Punjab involving fatal attacks, harassment and alleged suicide involving activists, officials said. Matters referenced include action in the attack on Bikramjit Singh and Nishan Singh Gurmukh Singh in Mari Panwan, Parwinder Singh Jhota’s killing in Mansa, and the alleged suicide of Gulzar Singh, father of a substance-abuse victim.

articles.headline: Lovers get death sentence for staging snakebite killing
articles.blurb: A Meerut court sentenced Ravita Kashyap and her lover Amardeep to death for murdering her husband Amit Kashyap on the night of April 12 last year and placing a snake on his body to fake a snakebite death; autopsy showed strangulation. Family members initially believed it was a snakebite; Additional District and Sessions Judge Jaiveer Singh Nagar delivered the verdict after prosecutors said the pair conspired after Amit objected to their affair.

articles.headline: Maha court sentences man to death for 4-yr-old’s rape, murder
articles.blurb: A Maharashtra court sentenced Vijay Khairnar to death as “rarest of the rare” for the November 16, 2025, sexual assault and murder of a four-and-a-half-year-old girl in Dongrale village, Nashik district. Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam said the court weighed gravity and circumstantial evidence from 24 witnesses; police filed a 425-page chargesheet in 23 days and CM Devendra Fadnavis announced Rs 10 lakh assistance for the family.

articles.headline: SC stays Twisha Sharma death trial, considers Delhi transfer
articles.blurb: The Supreme Court stayed the Bhopal sessions trial in former model Twisha Sharma’s unnatural death case and issued notices to the CBI, husband Samarth Singh and mother-in-law Giribala Singh on a transfer plea by father Navnidhi Sharma. Twisha, 33, was found hanging at her Katara Hills marital home on May 12; her family alleged dowry harassment while in-laws claimed drug addiction; the apex court had taken suo motu cognisance amid fairness concerns.

articles.headline: Cousin gets bail in Zubeen Garg death case
articles.blurb: The Gauhati High Court on Friday granted bail, with conditions, to Zubeen Garg’s cousin Sandipan, a DSP arrested in the cultural icon’s alleged murder case, along with female bandmate Amritprabha Mahanta. Sandipan, facing culpable homicide not amounting to murder and criminal conspiracy, had been in judicial custody since October 8 last year.

articles.headline: Microchip solution for stray dog management in Keralam
articles.blurb: Bengaluru-based DataPower Technologies is piloting ‘Shvan Suraksha’ microchipping of stray dogs with vaccination in Kasargod municipality and Wayanad’s Pandinjaratha and Muppainadu gram panchayats to track vaccination, sterilisation and hotspots. About 170 dogs have been chipped in Kasargod toward covering over 1,000 with CSR support, municipal chairperson Shahina Salim said.

articles.headline: Gunman kills 4 in US school
articles.blurb: A 16-year-old shot through locked doors into Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday, killing three children aged 5, 8 and 11 and a teacher; a person at the scene who followed him inside shot the attacker, who was found dead minutes after the first report. Another child aged 7 and a 54-year-old teacher were critically injured; the school had 459 students from kindergarten through fifth grade.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy blasts Trump’s diesel deal with Russia
articles.blurb: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticised US President Donald Trump’s diesel deal easing sanctions on Russia, saying it puts money in Putin’s pocket, and sought European backing at an EU summit in Brussels. He requested an extra €70 billion next year for defence; Russian drone strikes on Kharkiv killed three and left hundreds of thousands without power, while European Council chief Antonio Costa said it was no time to withdraw Ukraine support or ease Russia sanctions.

articles.headline: Pakistan to chair IMF, World Bank boards next year
articles.blurb: Pakistan was named incoming chair of the IMF and World Bank Boards of Governors for 2027, its first time since 1953, with Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema appointed at the 2026 Annual Meetings in Bangkok. Pakistan is engaged with the IMF under a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility and a $1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility.

articles.headline: US weighs using ‘mother of all bombs’ against Iran
articles.blurb: A report said the US military is considering using the GBU-43/B MOAB, the largest non-nuclear bomb in its arsenal, against Iran’s energy and nuclear sites subject to President Trump’s approval, as the war enters its eighth month. Trump told Newsmax the weapon is not nuclear; the ~21,600-pound MOAB was first used in combat in April 2017 against an ISIS tunnel complex in Afghanistan.

articles.headline: Modi to visit Canada
articles.blurb: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Canada on December 11 and 12, the Indian High Commission in Ottawa said; Canadian PM Mark Carney confirmed talks covering Toronto and Ottawa and said the visit might be broadened.

articles.headline: FBI extradites most-wanted fraudster from India
articles.blurb: Manjeet Singh Bedi, a most-wanted fraudster accused of irregularities in US government schemes and arrested in India last month, was extradited to the US on Wednesday night, the Department of Justice said. FBI Director Kash Patel thanked US and Indian partners; prosecutors will seek detention pending trial.

articles.headline: China eyes curbs on AI, biotech, solar exports
articles.blurb: China’s Commerce and Science and Technology ministries proposed export bans and restrictions on AI, biotech and solar technologies, including core AI large-model tech trained on sensitive national data, AI agents for key infrastructure and defence, certain cell and gene therapy platforms, and some solar module production tech. The draft lists a further 26 technologies facing fresh restrictions amid the US–China tech race.

articles.headline: Why Saudi Arabia Struggles to Stop the Houthis
articles.blurb: An NYT analysis notes Saudi Arabia’s over-$82-billion annual military budget still struggles against cheap Houthi drones and missiles, citing mismatched Patriot/THAAD defences (interceptors ~$3 million vs drones $15,000–$25,000), south-facing radar blind spots, and a divided military. Fighting reignited in 2026 after a 2022 ceasefire, with recent attacks including an airport strike killing 13 and wounding over 300 and a October 13 hit on an Aramco building in Dhahran.

articles.headline: US trying to break up Canada, says Carney
articles.blurb: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney warned in Calgary that outside forces are working to break Canada so they can “own us,” urging Alberta voters not to back a Monday referendum step toward a future separation vote amid US trade pressure and threats to make Canada a 51st state. He said a vote against unity would mean years of division and uncertainty.

articles.headline: Nepal: Preparations underway for PM Balendra Shah’s India visit
articles.blurb: Preparations are underway for Nepal PM Balendra Shah’s first official bilateral visit to India, though dates and agenda are not finalised; he received an invitation from PM Narendra Modi when his government formed in March. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said the trip could follow major Hindu festivals ending around mid-November.

articles.headline: Stocks end higher for 2nd day
articles.blurb: Sensex rose 413.66 points (0.56%) to 74,729.27 and Nifty 148.80 points (0.65%) to 23,146.15 on Friday, led by IT buying amid firm global trends. The rupee settled 10 paise higher at 94.89 against the US dollar for a sixth straight session, helped by RBI measures to curb spot dollar demand.

articles.headline: IDBI Bank transaction to close by March
articles.blurb: DIPAM Secretary Arunish Chawla said the strategic IDBI Bank transaction is expected to close by the end of the current financial year subject to RBI clearance. After the successful bidder submits technical papers and RBI clears it, the share purchase agreement will be signed.

articles.headline: DataLEADS and JanAI plan 100 AI hubs
articles.blurb: DataLEADS and JanAI signed an MoU to establish a proposed network of 100 Swasth AI Hubs across rural India to explore AI for community healthcare with medical colleges, research institutions and industry partners. JanAI founder Madan Padaki said the hubs and JanAI Cafés would help communities shape AI solutions in local languages.

articles.headline: MFs suspend subscriptions in gold FoFs
articles.blurb: More than a dozen mutual fund houses including SBI, HDFC, ICICI Prudential and Kotak temporarily suspended fresh subscriptions in gold fund-of-funds from Friday until further notice. Restrictions cover lump-sum investments, switch-ins and new SIPs and STPs in the affected schemes that invest in gold ETFs.

articles.headline: India needs to invest $2.4 tn in clean urban infra by 2050: FM
articles.blurb: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, citing a World Bank study at IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok, said India needs over $2.4 trillion for resilient low-carbon urban infrastructure by 2050 as urban population rises toward 951 million from about 480 million in 2020. She said the Urban Challenge Fund has Rs 1 lakh crore central assistance aiming to catalyse Rs 4 lakh crore investment, and NIIF’s government commitment was raised to Rs 60,000 crore with an additional Rs 30,000 crore.

articles.headline: India-Canada to sign CEPA soon, says Canadian minister
articles.blurb: Canada’s International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu said in Bengaluru that India and Canada are on track to conclude a CEPA this year, aiming to more than double two-way trade to $70 billion by 2030. Canada brought 300 delegates from 150 organisations; he cited KIA–YVR sister airport ties, Fairfax’s majority stake in IDBI Bank worth close to CAD 8 billion, and over 30 deals worth nearly CAD 300 million signed during the week.

articles.headline: ‘India-US trade pact would be concluded at earliest, in interest of global trade’
articles.blurb: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman expressed hope the India–US trade agreement would be concluded soon; Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said Thursday the first phase has been finalised and is in legal drafting. On China she flagged the trade imbalance and market-access curbs, and said India wants more rupee and local-currency trade settlements.

articles.headline: LTIM Q2 net profit down 4.6% QoQ to Rs 1,398 crore
articles.blurb: LTIM posted consolidated net profit of Rs 1,398 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, up marginally YoY but down 4.6% sequentially, with revenue of Rs 11,807.6 crore. EBIT was Rs 1,838.1 crore (margin 15.6%); the firm added 20 clients, AI revenue was 13.4% of sales, and order inflow was $1.26 billion.

articles.headline: Indian laws apply to all: Reliance breaks silence on Musk row
articles.blurb: Reliance Industries broke its silence on Elon Musk’s criticism of India’s satcom landscape, welcoming competition including Starlink but insisting every player must obey Indian laws; it cited Jio’s growth from zero customers in 2016 to over 530 million. The company said Jio’s own satellite services await clearances under the same process applied to Indian and foreign applicants.

articles.headline: Tech Mahindra Q2 profit rises 33%; board recommends 1:1 bonus shares
articles.blurb: Tech Mahindra reported a 32.74% jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 1,585.6 crore for Q2 FY27, with revenue up 15.6% to Rs 16,180.2 crore. The board recommended a 1:1 bonus issue—its first in 11 years—expected to be credited by December 15 as the company marks its 40th anniversary; CEO Mohit Joshi cited deal wins exceeding $1 billion in each of the last four quarters.

articles.headline: KWIN City: Plot allotments to begin by March, says minister
articles.blurb: Large and Medium Industries Minister M B Patil said Karnataka’s KWIN City project should see significant progress by February–March next year and directed KIADB to work round the clock with progress reports every 15 days. He ordered a dedicated on-site team to resolve land, road and drainage issues so facilities meet global standards for expected investors including IISc, universities, hospitals and start-ups.

articles.headline: Federal Bank net profit jumps 45% in Q2
articles.blurb: Federal Bank’s net profit rose 45.1% YoY to a record Rs 1,386 crore, with NII up 26.4% to Rs 3,153 crore and NIM at 3.32%. Total business stood at Rs 6.4 lakh crore; gross and net NPAs were at decade lows of 1.32% and 0.17%; the bank appointed Rajesh Varrier to its board.

articles.headline: Ambani taps massive Reliance workforce to boost Jio’s record IPO
articles.blurb: Mukesh Ambani is mobilising Reliance’s nearly 420,000 employees to invest in Jio Platforms’ IPO of up to Rs 30,200 crore, aiming for a valuation up to Rs 10.30 lakh crore, including early October salary release and outreach on demat accounts. Employee quota is up to Rs 500 crore at a 5% discount; subscription opens October 21–23 with the anchor book on October 19.

articles.headline: Grizzly clinches main event
articles.blurb: Somashekar-ward Grizzly, ridden by Rafique S K, won the A R Subramanya Raj Urs Memorial Trophy, the main event of the Mysuru races on Friday, beating Vibrant Queen, Mystikos and Absolutechallenger in 1-12.92. Other winners included Legendary Impact, Cauvery, Shamsheer, Star Of Light, Lg’s Star and Moonlight Scotch.

articles.headline: Pristine Glory for feature
articles.blurb: D Netto-trained Pristine Glory, to be ridden by Akshay Kumar, is fancied to win the Rani Rudrama Devi Trophy, the main Hyderabad race on Saturday; first race is at 1:35 pm. Day’s best tip is Love In Paris.

articles.headline: Party returns to Garden City
articles.blurb: India and West Indies play the series-deciding fifth T20I at M Chinnaswamy Stadium with the series tied 2-2 and rain a threat after the ground was under covers most of Friday. Bhuvneshwar Kumar has joined as injury cover for Arshdeep Singh; West Indies coach Daren Sammy said competing against the world’s best ticks progress boxes.

articles.headline: NZ tour: Split teams for ODIs; Akash returns
articles.blurb: Selectors announced split ODI squads for New Zealand plus a Test squad, with Rishabh Pant and Prasidh Krishna picked subject to fitness and Akash Deep returning for the two Tests; Jasprit Bumrah is rested from ODIs. Shreyas Iyer will captain the fourth and fifth ODIs with Ishan Kishan as deputy when Gill, Rahul and Kamboj miss those games for India A duty; ODIs run November 4–15 and Tests from November 19 in Wellington and November 27 in Christchurch.

articles.headline: Debutant Niki, veteran Deepti steer India home
articles.blurb: Debutant Niki Prasad (39 not out) and Deepti Sharma (49) added 82 as India recovered from 19 for four to beat Zimbabwe by four wickets in the opening Women’s T20I in Raipur, chasing 116 in 15.4 overs after Zimbabwe made 114 for five. Nyasha Gwanzura took 3-18; Deepti was Player of the Match; India lead the three-match series 1-0 with the second T20I on October 18.

articles.headline: Amruta enters final, Komal bags bronze
articles.blurb: Amruta Pujari of Solapur reached the women’s 72kg final at the under-23 World Wrestling Championships in Las Vegas after pinning China’s Wenjin Qiu in the semifinals; she will face Ukraine’s Iryna Zablotska for gold. Komal won bronze in 59kg over Kazakhstan’s Viktoriia Khusainova; Sweety remains in 53kg bronze contention via repechage.

articles.headline: Massive hike in assistance for NSFs hosting big events
articles.blurb: National Sports Federations can now get up to Rs 50 crore to organise international events, up from Rs 2 crore, under revised Sports Ministry ANSF guidelines aligned with India’s 2036 Olympic bid and 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad. Slabs include Rs 50 crore for disciplines finishing top 10 at Olympics/Worlds, Rs 20 crore for top 16, and Rs 3 crore depending on Asian Games participation.

articles.headline: India men start vs Germany, women face Britain
articles.blurb: India’s 2026-27 FIH Pro League home campaign opens with men versus Germany on February 13, then Argentina, Britain and Spain through February 28. The women open against Great Britain on February 23 and also face Spain through February 28.

articles.headline: K’taka squander advantage
articles.blurb: Karnataka blew a 2-0 lead to lose 2-3 to Uttar Pradesh in a senior men’s national hockey championship Pool A game in Jhansi. Captain Abharan Sudev and Majji Ganesh scored before Ashu Maurya pulled one back for UP in the 32nd minute.

articles.headline: Rachin takes leaf out of Kohli, Rohit’s books
articles.blurb: New Zealand batter Rachin Ravindra said he has modelled his batting on idols Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma, citing Kohli in bouncy conditions and Rohit against spin. In 2025 he scored 469 Test runs at 117.25 and in 2026 has 339 runs at 48.42; he called Jasprit Bumrah world-class and difficult to face in New Zealand.

articles.headline: BFC down Roots FC 4-1
articles.blurb: Bengaluru FC beat Roots FC 4-1 in the KSFA Karnataka Super Division at Bangalore Football Stadium; Ningthoukhongjam Rishi Singh and Nee Hang Subba scored early and S Chinmay and Chaphamayum Rohen Singh added late goals. Other results: Stride FC 2-2 Kodagu FC; Kickstart FC 1-0 South United FC.

articles.headline: Pacers Vidwath, Vyshak return; Shreyas to lead in next 2 games
articles.blurb: Karnataka named four changes for Ranji Trophy Group B matches against Saurashtra (Alur, Oct 18–21) and Tripura (Mysuru, Oct 26–29), with pacers Vidwath Kaverappa and Vyshak Vijaykumar returning and Rohan A Patil and S J Nikin Jose replacing KL Rahul and Smaran R, who join India A. Spinning all-rounder Shreyas Gopal will captain after Karnataka took only one point from a draw with Andhra.

articles.headline: Bengaluru FC renew rivalry with Chennaiyin
articles.blurb: Bengaluru FC host Chennaiyin FC at Sree Kanteerava Stadium on Saturday after a 3-2 win over Sporting Club Delhi; Chennaiyin arrive after a 1-1 draw at FC Goa. BFC are without Sivasakthi Narayanan; Chennaiyin miss Glan Martins, Vincy Barretto and Maheson Singh; Borja Martinez scored twice in the opener and Henno Koch headed the 89th-minute winner.

articles.headline: Blistering tons by Anvay, Dhruv power K’taka home
articles.blurb: Anvay Dravid (151) and Dhruv Krishnan (130) added 204 as Karnataka beat Gujarat by five wickets (VJD) in the Vinoo Mankad Trophy (U-19) in Vizianagaram after Gujarat posted 357/4. Karnataka reached 352/5 in 45.3 overs and were ahead on VJD when declared winners.

articles.headline: Young Jodar too hot for Ruud; Medvedev through
articles.blurb: Daniil Medvedev beat Tommy Paul 6-3, 1-6, 6-3 to reach the Shanghai Masters semifinals against 20-year-old Rafael Jodar, who recovered from a set down to beat Casper Ruud 4-6, 6-4, 6-3. At Wuhan, Iga Swiatek beat Ann Li 6-4, 6-1 to set up an all-Polish semi with Maja Chwalinska; Sonay Kartal beat world No. 6 Elina Svitolina 6-2, 2-6, 6-4.

articles.headline: 3 Indians eye the cut
articles.blurb: When round two of the DP World India Championship at Delhi Golf Club was suspended, Om Prakash Chauhan was tied 17th and Anirban Lahiri and Saptak Talwar tied 46th, all still in contention for the cut. Angel Hidalgo, Joost Luiten and Adrian Meronk shared the clubhouse lead at eight under on a weather-affected leaderboard.

articles.headline: Unnati equals U-23 100m record
articles.blurb: Karnataka’s Unnathi Aiyappa, representing Reliance, won the women’s 100m gold in 11.62 seconds, equalling Sakshi Champala’s meet record, on day one of the Indian Open U-23 Athletics Competition in Jaipur. Maharashtra’s Rushiprasad Desai set a men’s 100m meet record of 10.35 seconds; Dev Kumar Meena won pole vault gold at 5.30m.

articles.headline: Dominant K’taka in quarters
articles.blurb: Rachitha Hatwar (84) and Shreya Chavan (65) powered Karnataka to 168/3 before Kushi Suryakant (4/25) and Uma Kashvi (4/22) bowled Mumbai out for 110 as Karnataka won by 58 runs and reached the quarters of the BCCI Women’s U-19 T20 tournament in New Chandigarh.
